Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from this game where England registers a huge win while Netherlands slips further down. The action now moves to Bengaluru where New Zealand takes on Sri Lanka with qualification to the knockouts on the line. That game will begin be played on 9th November, Thursday at 2 pm IST (8.30 am GMT), but as you know, you can join us early for all the build-up to the match. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

Jos Buttler, the victorious skipper of England says that it was a great performance and they were desperate for the win. Mentions that it was a great start from Dawid Malan and the partnership between Ben Stokes and Chris Woakes was fantastic. On Stokes, he says that he is always there to stand up when they need someone to do that. Mentions that 339 was a really good score. Shares that the toss is an interesting aspect of the World Cup but feels that they have not done well even after winning the toss. On Woakes, he says that he is a skillful cricketer and sets the tone with the ball along with David Willey. On the game against Pakistan, he says that it is a huge game in what has been a disappointing tournament. Adds that they will prepare well and are looking forward to it.

Scott Edwards, the captain of Netherlands says that it is obviously a disappointing performance. Adds that they didn't start well with the ball but were able to pull things back in the middle overs but then let them get away with it at the death. Tells that is the same old story with the bat as the wicket was a good one and credits England for their batting. Mentions that it is about balance when chasing as you need to score quick runs in the Powerplay while also needing wickets in the middle. Says that they have been good in patches but they will need to do it for longer periods. Ends by saying that it will be an amazing atmosphere against India in Bengaluru and they are looking forward to it.

Ben Stokes is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his brilliant hundred. He says that he is more pleased to get the win than his knock. Adds that it has been a tough World Cup for them and it is nice to get back up. Shares that it was a typical Pune surface but felt that the balls bowled on a back of a length had tennis ball bounce. States he looked up to the scoreboard whenever he felt pressure and it certainly helped. On Chris Woakes, he says that he is a pretty experienced cricketer and a genuine all-rounder. Further adds that he showed tonight how great a cricketer he has been for the past two years. On whether he thought about going home for his knee surgery, he says that he does not want to leave his team hanging.
Presentation Time...

Earlier in the game, after electing to bat first, England posted a big total on the board courtesy of a nice half-century from Dawid Malan at the start but the main credit goes to an exceptional hundred from Ben Stokes who took his team out of trouble after struggling in the middle overs. He was also well supported by Chris Woakes who registered a fine fifty as well. Bas de Leede was the pick of the bowlers with three wickets while Aryan Dutt and Logan van Beek picked up a couple each. Paul van Meekeren chipped in with one too. While chasing, Netherlands did show some fight with a couple of good partnerships but they needed a lot more than that and the target proved to be too much for them in the end.

England, on the other hand, were all over the Dutch with Chris Woakes and David Willey both making the ball talk and moving it both ways and the batters had no answers to it. Both of them picked up a wicket and set the tone for them. They allowed a stand to build but a miscommunication between the batters gave them the opportunity to break it and they took with both hands. Adil Rashid then got another breakthrough in the middle overs to put their opponents further on the back foot. They also dropped a few chances but that didn't cost them much. Once Moeen Ali got rid off the Netherlands skipper which was also his first wicket in this World Cup, they were able to gain full control of the game. Ali and Rashid shared six wickets equally and absolutely ran through the lower order of the Dutch to confirm the win.

Netherlands got off to a very sluggish start as they found it hard to score runs against some quality pace bowling from England and lost a couple of wickets early on. Wesley Barresi struggled initially but he along with Sybrand Engelbrecht steadied the ship for a bit with a 55-run stand before the former lost his wicket due to a mix-up in the middle which was also their 10th run out in this World Cup which is an unwanted record for them. Their skipper, Scott Edwards came in after that but even before he could settle in, Sybrand was dismissed trying to up the ante. Then Teja Nidamanuru joined his captain and both of them slowly started to change gears and found the boundaries while also rotating the strike well with good running between the wickets. However, as the required rate was creeping up, Edwards failed to execute his big shot and lost his wicket and after that, the lower order fell like nine pins. Teja Nidamanuru remained unbeaten on 41 but they faced a massive defeat which now threatens their qualification chances for the Champions Trophy.

England finally win another game in this World Cup! This is only their second victory of the tournament and they completely outplayed Netherlands here to get a comprehensive win by 160 runs. These are also two important points to keep them in contention for direct qualification to the Champions Trophy 2025.

OUT! RUN OUT! A huge mixup and Wesley Barresi is gone! Netherlands' troubles with running between the wickets continue! Moeen Ali pulls the length back and bowls it on the pads, Wesley Barresi shimmies down the track now and flicks it in front of deep square leg. A yes-no situation between the two batters for the second run and Wesley Barresi is halfway down the track when Chris Woakes in the deep fires in the throw towards the non-striker's end. He throws it on the bounce and right above the stumps. Moeen Ali does the rest and catches Wesley Barresi well short of his crease despite the dive. This is the 10th instance of a Dutch batter being run out in this World Cup.

Commentary.Commentary: Close but not close enough! Commentary.Commentary: Almost another for Willey! This is touch fuller and around off, shapes away, Sybrand Engelbrecht looks to play at but gets an outside edge past first slip as Adil Rashid in the deep chases it and slides forward to push it back inside. Two runs taken!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: David Willey to Sybrand Engelbrecht, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Sybrand Engelbrecht makes his way out to the centre.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! David Willey strikes now! An absolute beauty of a delivery to get rid of Colin Ackermann who walks back for a duck. This is on a hard length and around off, threatens to swing in but angles away this time, Colin Ackermann plays for the shape in but only manages to get an outside edge behind where Jos Buttler makes no mistake. Netherlands lose their second wicket!
Commentary.Howout: c Jos Buttler b David Willey
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: David Willey to Colin Ackermann, OUT! c Jos Buttler b David Willey.

Commentary.Commentary: Full again and on off, Wesley Barresi opens the face of the bat and steers it wide of point where the fielder dives to his left to make a half-stop. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: David Willey to Wesley Barresi, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller one and around off, Wesley Barresi drives it straight to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: David Willey to Wesley Barresi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is on a good length and on middle, shaping in, Wesley Barresi stabs it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: David Willey to Wesley Barresi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and around middle, Colin Ackermann pats it down to the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Chris Woakes to Colin Ackermann, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Colin Ackermann walks in at number 3.

OUT! STRAIGHT TO THE FIELDER! Chris Woakes draws first blood! Max O'Dowd goes back for yet another low score in this World Cup. This is fuller in length and around middle, Max O'Dowd steps across and times his flick well again but uppishly towards mid on where Moeen Ali is standing well inside the ring and pouches is safely. Max O'Dowd is disappointed with himself and walks back to the hut. Netherlands lose their first wicket!
Commentary.Howout: c Moeen Ali b Chris Woakes
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Chris Woakes to Max O'Dowd, OUT! c Moeen Ali b Chris Woakes.

Commentary.Commentary: Pulls his length back a bit, on off, Max O'Dowd pushes it towards mid off.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Good shot! Chris Woakes lands this on a good length and around middle, angling in, Max O'Dowd stays there and uses his wrists nicely to flick it away through square leg with fine timing for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Chris Woakes to Max O'Dowd, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on off, Wesley Barresi knocks it towards mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: David Willey to Wesley Barresi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: David Willey nails the in-swinging yorker now, on middle, Wesley Barresi manages to dig it out well down the ground.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and around off, takes off a bit, Wesley Barresi gets surprised by the bounce as he looks to keep it out but misses and the ball goes past the outside edge again to the keeper.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! First boundary of the innings! This is full again and down the leg side again, Wesley Barresi looks to glance it away but gets an inside edge onto his thigh pads as the ball races towards the fine leg fence for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: David Willey to Wesley Barresi, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Goes fuller bit down the leg side, Wesley Barresi misses his flick as the ball goes off his pads to the keeper.

Commentary.Commentary: Excellent stuff from the England pacers! David Willey bowls this on a good length and around off, angling away, Wesley Barresi plays for the shape in but gets beaten on the outside edge.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on leg, Wesley Barresi clips it through square leg for one.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air..safe! This is a bit fuller and on middle, Max O'Dowd looks to flick but gets a leading edge just over and wide of mid off. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Chris Woakes to Max O'Dowd, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: How has that missed the stumps? Chris Woakes lands this on good length and around middle, this time it jags back in sharply with a bit of a bounce, Max O'Dowd gets cut in half as he looks to play at it and the ball just goes past the stumps behind where Jos Buttler dives to his left to collect it well.

Commentary.Commentary: This is pitched up and on middle, shaping in again, Wesley Barresi tucks it towards short mid-wicket.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be David Willey to steam in from the other end.
On a length and on middle, Max O'Dowd blocks it out.

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED AT SLIPS! Chris Woakes bowls this on a good length in the corridor of uncertainty, Wesley Barresi looks to push it away but gets an outside edge towards first slip where Joe Root dives to his left and tries to grab it with his outstretched left hand but spills it out. It was probably Jos Buttler's catch. Barresi gets an early life here as the batters also gets across for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Chris Woakes to Wesley Barresi, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: An appeal for caught behind, but turned down! The slips look confident and convinces Jos Buttler to take the review. This is fuller again and on off, moves away once more, Wesley Barresi tries to drive it away from the body but gets beaten on the outside edge as Jos Buttler collects it. Root appeals for it but UltraEdge shows nothing and England lose the review.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Chris Woakes to Wesley Barresi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tocuh fuller and on the sixth stump line, shaping away again, Wesley Barresi offers not shot at it.

Commentary.Commentary: BEAUTY! Chris Woakes lands this on a hard length and just around off, nips away just a shy bit, Wesley Barresi has a poke at it but withdraws his bat in the end. However, the ball was not far away from the outside edge.

Commentary.Commentary: This is on a good length and around off, shaping away again, Wesley Barresi lets it go to the keeper.

Commentary.Commentary: Movement straightaway from Chris Woakes! He starts with a full delivery, outside off, shaping further away, Wesley Barresi leaves it alone. Wided! Netherlands are underway with extras!
